messages:
Sara (support): Heads up — NovusPay reports failing webhooks after our private VPC NAT swap this morning (~05:38 UTC). Their firewall is rejecting requests because source IPs changed. 

Mike (netops): Which source IPs are they seeing on their side? We did an automated ENI/NAT replace during the autoscale window.

Sara (support): From their ticket: 
```
Remote firewall log: action=drop src=52.14.200.123 dst=10.0.2.45 proto=TCP reason=ip-not-in-allowlist
Customer says they only allow 52.14.199.88
```

Anish (oncall): That fits a SNAT rebind. Two quick asks: can you paste the webhook request headers (esp. X-Forwarded-For) and the name they're allowlisting (IP vs hostname)? Also what's the TTL on that DNS if they're using a hostname?

Sara (support): They only had the IP (52.14.199.88) in their rules. They told me they resolve our hostname once a day but pinned the IP manually in the firewall. TTL unknown.

Lena (eng): Confirming we rotated the NAT ENI pool in eu-west-1 at 05:38 UTC for that VPC. Old egress block ~52.14.199.0/24, new ephemeral block moved into 52.14.200.0/24. This was expected but should be transparent for customers that use DNS names.

Mike (netops): Likely two problems colliding: (1) NovusPay pinned an IP instead of domain, (2) their firewall caching + DNS TTL caused stale mapping. Quick repro steps for them / us:

```
# check what we now resolve
dig +short egress.novus.redwood-inference.net
# simulate customer firewall pin to current IP
curl -v https://hooks.novuspay.example/path --resolve hooks.novuspay.example:443:52.14.200.123
```

Anish (oncall): Also check port ranges — SNAT port mapping differences can cause backend failures if their firewall is also doing stateful checks. Not just IP mismatch.

Sara (support): NovusPay just replied: they confirm the firewall rule is a single IP entry (hardcoded). They can add a /24 but are reluctant. They asked if we can guarantee stable egress for their org.

Lena (eng): Short-term mitigations: we can temporarily rebind traffic for NovusPay to the previous ENI (sticky egress) for the next 6 hours while they update their rules. Long-term we should offer one of two options: (A) provide static egress IPs (Reserved Egress) per-customer, or (B) recommend domain-based allowlisting and advertise our egress hostname with a low TTL.

Mike (netops): For the immediate workaround I can add an outbound policy to pin NovusPay's VPC traffic to the old ENI pool. That requires a quick infra change (non-disruptive) but needs approval. I'll schedule it now.

deploy-bot: [audit] NAT rotation event recorded: change_id=chg-2026-07-15-418, user=infra-autoscale, time=2026-07-15T05:38:12Z, old_range=52.14.199.0/24, new_range=52.14.200.0/24.

Anish (oncall): Action items:
- Sara: ask NovusPay to temporarily allow 52.14.200.0/24 or to add the egress hostname to their firewall rules (domain-based) and flush DNS caches.
- Mike: implement pinning to previous ENI for 6h and confirm once done.
- Lena: follow up with product to fast-track Reserved Egress/IPs offering for customers with strict allowlists.

Sara (support): I'll relay and ask them to test after we pin. NovusPay asked for a quick verification command they can run from their firewall/admin host:
```
# validate source IP seen by NovusPay webhook endpoint
curl -s -X POST https://hooks.novuspay.example/inspect -d '{}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' | jq '.source_ip'
```

Mike (netops): Pin applied (done). Please verify. I left a note: chg-2026-07-15-418 -> rollback path exists.

Sara (support): NovusPay confirms success — traffic is accepted again and their firewall logs now show 52.14.199.88. They will update rules to allow 52.14.200.0/24 or switch to domain-based allowlist during their maintenance window tonight. :thumbsup:

Lena (eng): Filing follow-up ticket to product for Reserved Egress feature and a doc snippet about best practices for allowlisting (recommend domain allowlist + recommended TTLs).

Anish (oncall): Marking incident resolved for now. If NovusPay runs into any more flapping after they change their rules, reopen and we'll evaluate offering a permanent static egress.

Sara (support): Thanks team, closing loop with customer and will attach the change_id and repro steps to the support ticket.
